For elastic scattering the partial-wave expansion of the scattering amplitude is  

f(θ)= 1/(2ik)  Σ_{l=0}^{∞} (2l+1)(e^{2iδ_l}-1) P_l(cos θ)

Along the incident-beam (forward) direction θ = 0, so P_l(1)=1 for all l and

f(0)= 1/(2ik)  Σ_{l=0}^{4} (2l+1)(e^{2iδ_l}-1)       (higher-l phases are neglected).

1.  Compute S_l ≡ e^{2iδ_l}-1  

   l = 0 : δ_0 = 90° → 2δ = 180° → S_0 = –2 + 0i  
   l = 1 : δ_1 = 67°  → 2δ = 134° → S_1 = –1.694658 + 0.719340 i  
   l = 2 : δ_2 = 55°  → 2δ = 110° → S_2 = –1.342020 + 0.939693 i  
   l = 3 : δ_3 = 30°  → 2δ = 60°  → S_3 = –0.500000 + 0.866025 i  
   l = 4 : δ_4 = 13°  → 2δ = 26°  → S_4 = –0.101206 + 0.438371 i  

2.  Form the weighted sum  

   Σ (2l+1) S_l  =  
   1(–2+0i) + 3(–1.694658+0.719340i)  
   +5(–1.342020+0.939693i) +7(–0.500000+0.866025i)  
   +9(–0.101206+0.438371i)

   = (–18.204828) + i 16.863859 .

3.  Wave number k for a 50 MeV (non-relativistic approximation used in the problem) electron:

   p = √(2mE) = √(2·0.511 MeV·50 MeV) ≈ 7.146 MeV/c  
   k = p/(ħc) = 7.146 / 197.327 ≈ 0.03621 fm⁻¹  

   Hence 1/(2k) = 1/0.07242 ≈ 13.8099 fm.

4.  Imaginary part of f(0):

   Im f(0) = –(Re Σ)/(2k) = –(–18.204828)·13.8099  
           ≈ 18.204828·13.8099  
           ≈ 2.5127×10² fm.

Thus  

Im f(θ=0) ≈ 2.51×10² fm ≃ 251.3 fm.

The value matches option (A).

Answer: A
